provenance: Hand-recorded answers in the shape the version 5 roles return (no model was called): a visual direction written as territories, a designer's ideas turn, and two selection answers.

deliverable.concept: concept-1: The song is the object you hold.

treatments.name: The hook you can hold
treatments.visualIdea: The best eight bars of a song become a physical object the musician picks up; it fits a tool that cuts the hook out of a mix.
treatments.twoSeconds: That the best part of my song can be found and lifted out at once.
treatments.productRole: The interface is the hand that lifts the hook.
treatments.makingTechnique: A rendered 3D object for the hook, with a code-built interface around it, because the object must look real and the interface exact.
treatments.success: The viewer reads the promise before the headline.

treatments.name: Before and after the cut
treatments.visualIdea: A long waveform collapses into one bright slice; the brand's restraint makes the cut feel precise.
treatments.productRole: The product is the cut itself.
treatments.makingTechnique: Code-built graphics only, because the waveform and the interface are drawn shapes.
treatments.success: The cut is the first thing the eye lands on.

treatments.name: The room goes quiet
treatments.visualIdea: A crowded studio photograph fades except the eight bars that matter.
treatments.productRole: The product decides what stays lit.
treatments.makingTechnique: A photograph with a code-built interface over it, because the room must feel lived in.
treatments.success: The viewer feels the relief of the quiet.

productionConstraints: The interface is built in code from the brand's components.

ideas:
Rough ideas first: a hook as an object; a cut in a waveform; a quiet room.

Pushed further, each now has one strong turn.

IDEA 1: The viewer sees a hand lifting a glowing eight-bar block out of a dense mix. Turn: the block is heavy, the rest is air. Way of making: rendered 3D object in a code-built interface. It stops the scroll because the promise is literally in your hand.

IDEA 2: The viewer sees an endless waveform snap shut around one bright slice. Turn: the slice keeps playing. Way of making: code-built graphics. It stops the scroll because the motion of the cut is the product.

IDEA 3: The viewer sees a packed studio fall dark except one lit bar. Turn: silence. Way of making: photograph with code-built interface. It stops the scroll because the quiet is unexpected in a music ad.
